pathways.name: B Cell Depletion & CNS Compartmentalized Inflammation
pathways.description: B cells play a central role in MS beyond antibody production: they present antigen to T cells, produce pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF, GM-CSF), and form ectopic lymphoid follicles in the meninges. Anti-CD20 therapies (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, ublituximab) deplete CD20+ B cells but spare CD20- plasma cells and pro-B cells, allowing B cell reconstitution. Meningeal B cell follicles in progressive MS are associated with cortical demyelination and neurodegeneration.

pathways.name: S1P Receptor Modulation / Lymphocyte Sequestration
pathways.description: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) is a bioactive lipid mediator that regulates lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes via S1P receptor 1 (S1PR1) gradient sensing. S1P receptor modulators (fingolimod, siponimod, ozanimod, ponesimod) cause S1PR1 internalization, trapping autoreactive lymphocytes in lymph nodes and preventing their migration to the CNS. S1P5 modulation on oligodendrocytes may additionally promote remyelination.

pathways.name: Integrin / Adhesion Blockade — Blood-Brain Barrier
pathways.description: Lymphocyte migration across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a critical step in MS lesion formation. α4β1 integrin (VLA-4) on lymphocytes binds VCAM-1 on activated brain endothelial cells, enabling firm adhesion and transendothelial migration. Natalizumab blocks this interaction, preventing lymphocyte entry into the CNS. This pathway is shared across neuroinflammatory diseases and provides a template for CNS-specific immunotherapy.

pathways.name: Th17 / IL-17 Pro-inflammatory Axis
pathways.description: Th17 cells (CD4+IL-17A+) are key drivers of CNS autoimmunity in MS. IL-23 from dendritic cells and macrophages drives Th17 differentiation via STAT3/RORγt. Th17 cells produce IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-21, IL-22, and GM-CSF. IL-17 disrupts BBB tight junctions, promotes neutrophil recruitment, and synergizes with TNF in oligodendrocyte cytotoxicity. The IL-23/Th17 axis is genetically linked to MS through IL12B, IL23R, STAT3, and TYK2 variants.
therapeutic_targets: Potential: anti-IL-17 (secukinumab — failed in MS, may worsen)

pathways.name: NF-κB / NRF2 Oxidative Stress Pathway
pathways.description: Oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction are key drivers of neurodegeneration in progressive MS. NF-κB activation in microglia and macrophages drives pro-inflammatory cytokine production, while NRF2 (NFE2L2) is the master regulator of antioxidant defense. Dimethyl fumarate and diroximel fumarate activate NRF2, inducing expression of antioxidant enzymes (NQO1, HO-1, GST). The NRF2 pathway also suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammation. This pathway is particularly important in progressive MS where oxidative damage accumulates.

pathways.name: Type I Interferon & JAK-STAT Signaling
pathways.description: Type I interferon (IFN-α/β) signaling through IFNAR1/IFNAR2 activates JAK1/TYK2 → STAT1/STAT2 → ISGF3 transcription. Paradoxically, IFN-β is therapeutic in MS, while type I IFN (IFN-α) drives pathology in SLE. IFN-β shifts the cytokine balance from Th1/Th17 toward Th2/IL-10, reduces MMP-9 expression, and restores BBB integrity. TYK2 mediates both type I IFN (protective) and IL-12/IL-23 (pathogenic) signaling, making it a complex therapeutic target.
therapeutic_targets: deucravacitinib (TYK2i — in development for autoimmune disease)

pathways.name: BTK Signaling in B Cells & Myeloid Cells
pathways.description: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) is a critical signaling kinase downstream of the BCR in B cells and FcγR/FcεR in myeloid cells (microglia, macrophages). In MS, BTK inhibitors (evobrutinib, tolebrutinib) offer a dual mechanism: (1) inhibit BCR-mediated B cell activation in the periphery, and (2) inhibit FcR-mediated microglial activation within the CNS. CNS penetration is essential — non-CNS-penetrant BTKis may not address smoldering compartmentalized inflammation driving progression.

pathways.name: Th17 / IL-23 Autoimmune Axis
pathways.description: Th17 cells key drivers of CNS autoimmunity. IL-23 essential for Th17 pathogenicity.

pathways.name: Blood-Brain Barrier & Immune Cell Trafficking
pathways.description: BBB crossing is critical in MS. Natalizumab blocks VLA-4/VCAM-1.
